question: Which sub-discipline of pharmacology describes what the BODY does to a drug (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion)?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Pharmacokinetics (PK) studies how the body handles a drug through ADME processes.
Pharmacodynamics (PD) describes what the drug does to the body — its mechanism of action and effects on receptors.
Pharmacognosy is the study of drugs derived from natural sources such as plants and minerals — not the body's handling of a drug.
Pharmacotherapeutics is the clinical application of drugs to treat disease — it does not describe the body's processing of a drug.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the five pharmacology sub-disciplines: PK (body acts on drug), PD (drug acts on body), pharmacognosy, pharmacotherapeutics, and clinical pharmacology.
Well done! PK = what the body does to the drug; PD = what the drug does to the body.
